title: hq goal new: start a goal in one command
acceptance: `hq goal new <name> [--title <text>] [--from <rev>]` creates branch goal/<name> from main (or from <rev>) and a linked worktree at <repo>.goals/<name>, a sibling of the repository directory
The goal branch's first commit adds goals/<name>.json with title, acceptance (empty list), shelved (empty list) and known_issues (empty list); the commit message is "goal <name>: start"

It refuses, changing nothing: a name that is not lowercase letters, digits and dashes (the same rule as hq approve); an existing goal/<name> branch; an existing worktree path; a --from that is not a commit
It prints the worktree path and the branch on success and exits 0; on refusal it prints why and exits non-zero
End-to-end tests in hq/test with a real git repository cover success and every refusal
known_issues: Two concurrent `hq goal new` runs with the same name can both pass the checks; the one whose `git worktree add` fails then rolls back the shared branch and worktree, deleting the other run's goal (Codex P1, round 3). Accepted as a detail on 2026-10-23: single user, no concurrent runs. Fix: roll back only what this run created.
